subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes:
PB55 FOLD (2026-10-15, owner decision 2026-08-08 'THE RULE IS THE UNIT'): the transcription printed this rule's nested list(s) at column 0, so 8 sub-item(s) held rows of their own; indented at their measured printed level, they are this rule's body and their adjudications are folded here, nothing dropped.

[the rule's own record before the fold]
ONE decoder and ONE builder answer SR14 for both classes (kb/Work PB770), because SR14 a is stated once above the b-series and the c-series and the two series differ only in the operand's literal class. a) duplicate character -> COBOL1906 on both arms, recovery keeping the first specification (negatives pb770-alphabet-duplicate-character, -national-duplicate, -syn-definition-1849; fact DuplicateCharacter_IsSR14a_OnBothArms). b1/c1) BOTH halves of one sentence - the UNSIGNED half (fact SignedOrdinal_IsSR14b1c1_UnsignedHalf, both arms: int.TryParse accepts a leading sign, so +5 read as ordinal 5 and only a NEGATIVE value was caught by the range half, a different rule answering for this one) and the range 1..65,536 over the native set of the clause's class (negative -ordinal-out-of-range; fact NationalOrdinal_OutsideTheNativeSet_IsSR14c1, both bounds). b2/c2) the noninteger literal's class (negative -noninteger-literal; fact NationalNonintegerLiteral_OfTheWrongClass_IsSR14c2, an alphanumeric literal in the national branch and a noninteger numeric literal). b3/c3) one character under THROUGH or ALSO, BOTH phrases (negative -multichar-thru-operand; fact NationalMultiCharacterOperand_UnderThroughOrAlso_IsSR14c3). b4/c4) DERIVED, not separately checked: a) makes every specified character distinct and distinct characters of a set cannot outnumber the set, so a phrase that satisfies a) cannot specify more characters than the native set contains. DistinctCharacters_AreAccepted_OnBothArms is the positive control against a regression that rejects every literal phrase.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L2.1 = §12.3.7.3 14) b) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR14 b)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each numeric literal shall be an unsigned integer and shall have a value within the range of one through the maximum number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set' -> OK 14) 1.). BOTH halves are enforced at every magnitude: the ordinal is read by THE ONE integer reader IntegerOperandRules.HostValue (saturating), so an integer too long for an int is held to the ordinal range rule, never to the noninteger-literal class rule (SR14 b2). SpecialNamesOrdinalReaderDriftTests forbids a second host-integer parse in DataBinder.Switches.cs.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L2.2 = §12.3.7.3 14) b) 2.: CONFORMS]
Rule (SR14 b)2): 'Each noninteger literal shall be an alphanumeric literal.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). OperandLiteralClass classifies by the literal's parsed prefix (CobolLiteral.ClassOf), so: l22_nat (N"A"), l22_natx (NX"0041"), l22_bool (B"1"), l21_decimal (66.0) -> COBOL1906 SR14 b2; l22_word (a bare word ZOT) -> refused naming SR14 b2 / GR10; l22_hex_ok (X"43" X"42", alphanumeric hexadecimal format) accepted and positioned C,B. Figurative constants map through GR10 (l23_fig_thru SPACE THRU "A" accepted - GR10 makes SPACE one character). Existing negative conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb770-alphabet-noninteger-literal (`1.5 ALSO 4`) pins the refusal. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (SR14 b)2)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L2.3 = §12.3.7.3 14) b) 3.: CONFORMS]
Rule (SR14 b)3): 'Each alphanumeric literal, when a THROUGH or ALSO phrase is specified, shall be one character in length.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). OneCharacterOperands runs whenever thru || ALSO: l23_thru_multi ("AB" THRU "C"), l23_also_multi ("A" ALSO "BC"), l23_hex_thru_multi (X"4142" THRU X"43" - checked on the DECODED length), l23_allfig_also (ALSO ALL "BC") -> COBOL1906 SR14 b3; the unconstrained case l23_plain_multi_ok ("DCB" without THRU/ALSO) builds D,C,B at positions 1-3 and ordinal ranges (l23_ordinal_thru_ok 69 THRU 67) are unaffected. Pinned by conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb770-alphabet-multichar-thru-operand. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (SR14 b)3)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L2.4 = §12.3.7.3 14) b) 4.: CONFORMS]
Rule (SR14 b)4): 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). (The row text's trailing 'c) When the NATIONAL phrase is specified:' is the next sub-item's heading captured by the catalog, not part of this rule.) Enforced by construction, as the code's own remark says: SR14 a) ('A given character shall not be specified more than once in that ALPHABET clause', cite OK §12.3.7.3 14)) is checked in Assign (probe l24_dup `"A" THRU "C" "B"` -> COBOL1906 SR14 a), every ordinal is range-checked to the 65,536-unit set, so the specified characters are distinct members of that set and cannot outnumber it. Verified by reading plus the a)/b1 probes; no test pins b4 itself (the SR14 a tests - conformance:cases/12.3.7-SPECIAL-NAMES/pb770-alphabet-duplicate-character - pin the mechanism, not this rule), so test-ref empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (SR14 b)4) | code-location as adjudicated: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#AlphabetLiteralPhrase (Assign - the SR14 a duplicate check)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L3.1 = §12.3.7.3 14) c) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR14 c)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each numeric literal shall be an unsigned integer and shall have a value within the range of one through the maximum number of characters in the native national character set' -> OK 14) 1.). The national arm reads its ordinal through the same ONE reader as the alphanumeric arm, so 0, 65537, 2147483648 and a 31-digit literal are all refused under SR14 c1.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L3.2 = §12.3.7.3 14) c) 2.: CONFORMS]
Rule (SR14 c)2): 'Each noninteger literal shall be a national literal.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). l32_alnum ("A") and l32_hexalnum (X"41") -> COBOL1906 SR14 c2; l32_nx_ok (`NX"0043" N"B" N"A"` as PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL) accepted and orders C<B<A, so N"A" > N"C" prints A>C - the national hexadecimal format is decoded as its character. Pinned by the conformance-test named.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L3.3 = §12.3.7.3 14) c) 3.: CONFORMS]
Rule (SR14 c)3): 'Each national literal, when a THROUGH or ALSO phrase is specified, shall be one character in length.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). l33_thru_multi (N"AB" THRU N"C") and l33_also_multi (N"A" ALSO N"BC") -> COBOL1906 SR14 c3, also at --std 2002 (l3_2002); l33_plain_multi_ok (N"CBA" with no phrase) accepted. The ONE OneCharacterOperands check serves both arms. Pinned by the conformance-test named.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L3.4 = §12.3.7.3 14) c) 4.: CONFORMS]
SR14 c)4 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set.' -> OK 12.3.7.3 14) 4.). The code has no explicit count test, and none is needed: the native national set is the 65,536 UTF-16 code units (CONFORMANCE DOC-A.1-33; CollatingTable.Repertoire), every operand decodes to a character of that set (the SR14 c1 ordinal range and the c2 class rule in LiteralPhraseOperand), and SR14 a (a character specified more than once -> COBOL1906, Assign in AlphabetLiteralPhrase, both arms) refuses any repeat, so no conforming source can specify more than 65,536 characters. probe dir: out/probe/special-names-p2/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). AL1 `ALPHABET NA FOR NATIONAL IS 1 THRU 65536` (the whole set) compiles and runs; AL2 adds N"A" and draws COBOL1906 SR14 a. So the count bound is enforced through SR14 a. No test targets c4 by name (AlphabetLiteralPhraseTests covers c1/c2/c3 and SR14 a on both arms), so test-ref is empty.
